Rio's Botanical Garden covers 137 hectares at the foot of Corcovado. It was founded by King João VI in 1808 and is home to more than 7,000 plant species.

The route begins along an avenue of 134 royal palms stretching approximately 750 metres. You can then see orchids, bromeliads, cacti, tall bamboo and ponds with giant Amazon water lilies. Toucans and other birds can be spotted in the treetops, and monkeys sometimes appear on the branches.

The excursion lasts approximately 4 hours.

## Brazilian Side of Iguazu Falls

From Foz do Iguaçu, you will travel to the waterfalls on the Brazilian side of the national park. The walking route follows the Iguazu River canyon, opening up panoramic views of the cascades amid tropical forest.

On the way to the viewpoints near Devil's Throat, you will see numerous waterfalls. Water thunders into the gorge, spray rises above the river, and rainbows appear in the mist when the sun shines. Different points along the route offer views of the cascades and the surrounding vegetation of the park.

After the excursion, you will return to your hotel on the Brazilian side.

You will see the 67-metre Obelisk on Avenida 9 de Julio, Plaza de Mayo, Plaza San Martín and Plaza del Congreso. The route follows Avenida Corrientes and Avenida de Mayo.

The historic neighbourhoods of La Boca, San Telmo and Monserrat give way to Palermo and Recoleta. In modern Puerto Madero, the city meets its former port docks. The tour then introduces you to Lezama Park and Tres de Febrero Park.

The city tour concludes with the financial and commercial centre and a football stadium. The specific stadium and whether an interior visit is possible are confirmed when the programme is agreed.
